literal: The Tiele of Shu rebelled in succession.
idiomatic: The Tiele of Shu rebelled in succession.

literal: An edict made Jiangyang Wang Ji, General Who Pacifies the North, commander-in-chief of the northern punitive campaign.
idiomatic: An edict made Jiangyang Wang Ji, General Who Pacifies the North, commander-in-chief of the northern punitive campaign.

literal: On renwu day the state of Goryeo sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: On the renwu day the state of Goryeo sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Ninth month, day jihai: because Xiao Luan had died, rites forbade attacking during mourning; an edict ordered the banners turned back.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the jihai day, because Xiao Luan had died, rites forbade attacking during mourning; an edict ordered the banners turned back.

literal: On gengzi day he still led the northern campaign against rebel barbarians.
idiomatic: On the gengzi day he still led the northern campaign against rebel barbarians.

literal: On bingwu day the imperial carriage set out from Xuanhu.
idiomatic: On the bingwu day the court set out from Xuanhu.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day jiyou first of month: partial amnesty for the two Yu provinces below capital punishment; the people's field rent was remitted one year.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the jiyou day, the new moon, a partial amnesty was granted for the two Yu provinces below capital punishment; the people's field rent was remitted one year.

literal: Eleventh month, day xinsi: he visited Ye.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the xinsi day, he visited Ye.

literal: Twelfth month, day jiayin: because Jiangyang Wang Ji had pacified the Tiele, an edict ordered withdrawal of the army.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the jiayin day, because Jiangyang Wang Ji had pacified the Tiele, an edict ordered withdrawal of the army.

literal: Twenty-third year, spring, first month, day wuyin first of month: the court assembled the ministers; because the Emperor's illness had abated, longevity was celebrated with a great feast in the Chengluan Hall.
idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, in the first month of spring, on the wuyin day, the new moon, the court assembled the ministers; because the emperor's illness had abated, longevity was celebrated with a great feast in the Chengluan Hall.

literal: Day renwu.
idiomatic: On the renwu day.

literal: He visited the shrine of Ximen Bao, then followed the Zhang River and returned.
idiomatic: He visited the shrine of Ximen Bao, then followed the Zhang River and returned.

literal: Xiao Baojuan dispatched Grand Marshal Chen Xianda to invade Jing province.
idiomatic: Xiao Baojuan dispatched Grand Marshal Chen Xianda to invade Jing province.

literal: On guiwei day, an edict ordered Forward General Yuan Ying to attack him.
idiomatic: On the guiwei day an edict ordered Forward General Yuan Ying to attack him.

literal: On yiyou day the imperial carriage set out from Ye; on wuxu day it returned from Ye.
idiomatic: On the yiyou day the court set out from Ye; on the wuxu day it returned from Ye.

literal: On gengzi day announcement was made at the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain.
idiomatic: On the gengzi day announcement was made at the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain.

literal: On guimao day the ritual of drinking on return and recording merit was performed.
idiomatic: On the guimao day the ritual of drinking on return and recording merit was performed.

literal: On jiachen day a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On the jiachen day a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

literal: Grand Guardian Prince of Qi commandery Jian died.
idiomatic: Grand Guardian Prince of Qi commandery Jian died.

literal: Second month, day xinhai: Xianyang Wang Xi, acting Grand Marshal, was made regular Grand Marshal.
idiomatic: In the second month, on the xinhai day, Xianyang Wang Xi, acting grand marshal, was made regular grand marshal.

literal: On guihai day Pengcheng Wang Xie was made Minister over the Masses; Yue-ling Wang Siyu's original fief was restored.
idiomatic: On the guihai day Pengcheng Wang Xie was made Minister over the Masses; Yue-ling Wang Siyu's original fief was restored.

literal: On guiyou day Xianda stormed and took the Maquan garrison.
idiomatic: On the guiyou day Xianda stormed and took the Maquan garrison.

literal: Third month, day gengchen: the imperial carriage marched south to attack.
idiomatic: In the third month, on the gengchen day, the emperor marched south to attack.

literal: On guiwei day he halted at Liangcheng.
idiomatic: On the guiwei day he halted at Liangcheng.

literal: On jiashen day, because Shunyang was besieged in grave peril, an edict ordered Zhenwu General Murong Pingcheng to lead five thousand horsemen to the rescue.
idiomatic: On the jiashen day, because Shunyang was besieged in grave peril, an edict ordered Zhenwu General Murong Pingcheng to lead five thousand horsemen to the rescue.

literal: On bingxu day the Emperor was unwell; Minister over the Masses Pengcheng Wang Xie attended his illness in the inner palace and for the time held all government.
idiomatic: On the bingxu day the emperor was unwell; Minister over the Masses Pengcheng Wang Xie attended his illness in the inner palace and for the time held all government.

literal: On dingyou day the imperial carriage reached Maquan.
idiomatic: On the dingyou day the court reached Maquan.

literal: An edict ordered Guangyang Wang Jia, General Who Guards the South, to cut the Jun mouth and block Xianda's route of return.
idiomatic: An edict ordered Guangyang Wang Jia, General Who Guards the South, to cut the Jun mouth and block Xianda's route of return.

literal: On wuxu day repeated battles defeated him; that night Xianda and Cui Huijing, Cao Hu, and others fled by night.
idiomatic: On the wuxu day repeated battles defeated him; that night Xianda and Cui Huijing, Cao Hu, and others fled by night.

literal: On jihai day their military stores, reckoned in the hundreds of millions, were seized and distributed to the six armies.
idiomatic: On the jihai day their military stores, reckoned in the hundreds of millions, were seized and distributed to the six armies.

literal: The generals pursued the fugitives to the Han River; those beheaded, captured, and drowned were eight or nine in ten; Left Army General Zhang Yuda of Baojuan and others were beheaded.
idiomatic: The generals pursued the fugitives to the Han River; those beheaded, captured, and drowned were eight or nine in ten; Left Army General Zhang Yuda of Baojuan and others were beheaded.

literal: [12] Rebel generals Cai Daofu and Cheng Gongqi led tens of thousands to abandon Shunyang and flee.
idiomatic: [12] Rebel generals Cai Daofu and Cheng Gongqi led tens of thousands to abandon Shunyang and flee.

literal: On gengzi day the Emperor's illness was severe; the imperial carriage halted north at Gutang Plain.
idiomatic: On the gengzi day the emperor's illness was severe; the court halted north at Gutang Plain.

literal: On jiachen day an edict granted death to Empress Feng.
idiomatic: On the jiachen day an edict granted death to Empress Feng.

literal: An edict ordered Minister over the Masses Xie to summon the crown prince from Luyang to ascend the throne.
idiomatic: An edict ordered Minister over the Masses Xie to summon the crown prince from Luyang to ascend the throne.

literal: An edict made Palace Attendant and Protector of the Army Beihai Wang Xiang Minister of Works, Wang Su, General Who Guards the South, Director of the Masters of Writing, Guangyang Wang Jia, General Who Guards the South, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Song Bian of the Masters of Writing Minister of Personnel, together with Palace Attendant and Grand Marshal Xi, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Rencheng Wang Cheng, and six others to assist in government.
idiomatic: An edict made Palace Attendant and Protector of the Army Beihai Wang Xiang minister of works, Wang Su, General Who Guards the South, director of the Masters of Writing, Guangyang Wang Jia, General Who Guards the South, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, Song Bian of the Masters of Writing minister of personnel, together with palace attendant and grand marshal Xi, right vice director of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Rencheng Wang Cheng, and six others to assist in government.

literal: Entrusted ministers said: "O you Grand Marshal, Minister of Works, Director of the Masters of Writing, left and right vice directors, and Minister of Personnel—Our founding ancestor's vast enterprise matches the four emblems in splendor; successive sages doubled the light, and the great mandate fell on Our dimness.
idiomatic: The entrusted ministers said, "O you grand marshal, minister of works, director of the Masters of Writing, left and right vice directors, and minister of personnel—our founding ancestor's vast enterprise matches the four emblems in splendor; successive sages doubled the light, and the great mandate fell on our dimness.

literal: With fearful care We think to continue the traces of the sage.
idiomatic: With fearful care we think to continue the traces of the sage.

literal: We moved the capital to Song's height and fixed the tripod at He and Luo, hoping to sweep Ou and Wu in the south and restore rites to the myriad states, to lift up the seven temples and succor the black-haired people below.
idiomatic: We moved the capital to Song's height and fixed the tripod at He and Luo, hoping to sweep Ou and Wu in the south and restore rites to the myriad states, to lift up the seven temples and succor the black-haired people below.

literal: Early trapped and extinguished, We could not long fulfill Our aim.
idiomatic: Early trapped and extinguished, we could not long fulfill our aim.

literal: [13] You ministers, well support and continue the heir, and exalt Our Wei house—is that not good?
idiomatic: [13] You ministers, well support and continue the heir, and exalt our Wei house—is that not good?

literal: You must exert yourselves!
idiomatic: You must exert yourselves!

literal: Summer, fourth month, day bingwu first of month: the Emperor died at the traveling palace on Gutang Plain, aged thirty-three.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the bingwu day, the new moon, the emperor died at the traveling palace on Gutang Plain. He was thirty-three.

literal: The death was kept secret; mourning was proclaimed at Luyang, then the court returned to the capital.
idiomatic: The death was kept secret; mourning was proclaimed at Luyang, then the court returned to the capital.

literal: The posthumous title was Emperor Xiaowen; the temple name was Gaozu.
idiomatic: The posthumous title was Emperor Xiaowen; the temple name was Gaozu.

literal: Fifth month, day bingshen: burial at Changling.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the bingshen day, burial at Changling.

literal: The Emperor from youth had utmost nature; at age four, when Emperor Xianwen once had an abscess, the Emperor personally sucked the pus.
idiomatic: The emperor from youth had utmost nature; at age four, when Emperor Xianwen once had an abscess, the emperor personally sucked the pus.

literal: At five he received the abdication and wept uncontrollably.
idiomatic: At five he received the abdication and wept uncontrollably.

literal: Emperor Xianwen asked the Emperor; the Emperor said: "The feeling for a parent in place of another cuts within the heart."
idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen asked the emperor; the emperor said, "The feeling for a parent in place of another cuts within the heart."

literal: Emperor Xianwen greatly marveled at him.
idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen greatly marveled at him.

literal: Empress Dowager Wencheng, because the Emperor was clever and sage, later might not favor the Feng clan, planned to depose the Emperor.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wencheng, because the emperor was clever and sage, later might not favor the Feng clan, planned to depose the emperor.

literal: Then in cold month, in single garment she closed the chamber, cut off food for three mornings, summoned Xianyang Wang Xi, intending to install him; Yuan Pi, Mu Tai, and Li Chong firmly remonstrated, and it stopped.
idiomatic: Then in a cold month, in a single garment she closed the chamber, cut off food for three mornings, summoned Xianyang Wang Xi, intending to install him; Yuan Pi, Mu Tai, and Li Chong firmly remonstrated, and it stopped.

literal: The Emperor at first had no resentment, but deeply owed virtue to Pi and the others.
idiomatic: The emperor at first had no resentment, but deeply owed virtue to Pi and the others.

literal: Cherishing his younger brothers, from start to finish there was never the slightest gap; he was thick and harmonious to the nine clans, with ritual respect all deep.
idiomatic: Cherishing his younger brothers, from start to finish there was never the slightest gap; he was thick and harmonious to the nine clans, with ritual respect all deep.

literal: Though toward great ministers he held the law and did not indulge, yet by nature he was broad and kind, and often showed pity and forbearance.
idiomatic: Though toward great ministers he held the law and did not indulge, yet by nature he was broad and kind, and often showed pity and forbearance.

literal: Those who served food once scalded the Emperor's hand with hot broth, and once filth of insects was found in the food—he laughed and forgave them both.
idiomatic: Those who served food once scalded the emperor's hand with hot broth, and once filth of insects was found in the food—he laughed and forgave them both.

literal: Eunuchs had earlier slandered the Emperor to the empress dowager; the empress dowager was greatly angered and beat the Emperor dozens of times; the Emperor silently bore it and did not explain himself.
idiomatic: Eunuchs had earlier slandered the emperor to the empress dowager; the empress dowager was greatly angered and beat the emperor dozens of times; the emperor silently bore it and did not explain himself.

literal: After the empress dowager died he also did not mind it.
idiomatic: After the empress dowager died he also did not mind it.

literal: In hearing and deciding affairs, none were not followed as good flows water.
idiomatic: In hearing and deciding affairs, none were not followed as good flows water.

literal: Pitying the hundred surnames, he constantly thought how to benefit them.
idiomatic: Pitying the hundred surnames, he constantly thought how to benefit them.

literal: Rites at Heaven and Earth, the five suburban sacrifices, and the ancestral temple at the two equinoxes—he always attended in person and was not weary of heat or cold.
idiomatic: Rites at Heaven and Earth, the five suburban sacrifices, and the ancestral temple at the two equinoxes—he always attended in person and was not weary of heat or cold.

literal: When the Masters of Writing submitted cases, he often examined them himself.
idiomatic: When the Masters of Writing submitted cases, he often examined them himself.

literal: Officials great and small—none did he not attend to, striving for thoroughness.
idiomatic: Officials great and small—none did he not attend to, striving for thoroughness.

literal: He often said: For anyone who is lord of men, the trouble is unevenness; one cannot push sincerity to govern things—if one can be even in sincerity, men of Hu and Yue can also be as close as brothers.
idiomatic: He often said, "For anyone who is lord of men, the trouble is unevenness; one cannot push sincerity to govern things—if one can be even in sincerity, men of Hu and Yue can also be as close as brothers."

literal: He often calmly told the historiographers: "Write the times straight, without concealing the state's shame.
idiomatic: He often calmly told the historiographers, "Write the times straight, without concealing the state's shame.

literal: When a lord takes authority and blessing on himself, if the historians again do not write, what is there to fear?"
idiomatic: When a lord takes authority and blessing on himself, if the historians again do not write, what is there to fear?"

literal: On northern and southern campaigns, when offices memorialized to repair the road, the Emperor said: "Roughly repair bridges so carts and horses may pass—that is enough; it is not necessary to cut grass and make it level."
idiomatic: On northern and southern campaigns, when offices memorialized to repair the road, the emperor said, "Roughly repair bridges so carts and horses may pass—that is enough; it is not necessary to cut grass and make it level."

literal: Whatever he constructed was because he had to; he did not harm the people's strength for unurgent matters.
idiomatic: Whatever he constructed was because he had to; he did not harm the people's strength for unurgent matters.

literal: Touring south of the Huai, it was as in the inner lands; when the military had to cut people's trees, silk was always left to pay the price; the people's rice and millet were nowhere trampled.
idiomatic: Touring south of the Huai, it was as in the inner lands; when the military had to cut people's trees, silk was always left to pay the price; the people's rice and millet were nowhere trampled.

literal: All taboo and exorcism formulas not recorded in the canonical classics were abolished.
idiomatic: All taboo and exorcism formulas not recorded in the canonical classics were abolished.

literal: He elegantly loved reading and did not release the scroll from his hand.
idiomatic: He elegantly loved reading and did not release the scroll from his hand.

literal: The meaning of the Five Classics—he read and could lecture at once; he studied without a teacher, probing their subtle depths.
idiomatic: The meaning of the Five Classics—he read and could lecture at once; he studied without a teacher, probing their subtle depths.

literal: Histories, traditions, and the hundred schools—none did he not cover.
idiomatic: Histories, traditions, and the hundred schools—none did he not cover.

literal: He was skilled in discussing Zhuangzi and Laozi, and especially refined in Buddhist meaning.
idiomatic: He was skilled in discussing Zhuangzi and Laozi, and especially refined in Buddhist meaning.

literal: His literary talent was rich; he loved to compose essays, poems, fu, inscriptions, and eulogies, composing as the mood moved.
idiomatic: His literary talent was rich; he loved to compose essays, poems, fu, inscriptions, and eulogies, composing as the mood moved.

literal: He had great literary power; on horseback he dictated by mouth, and when complete not one character was changed.
idiomatic: He had great literary power; on horseback he dictated by mouth, and when complete not one character was changed.

literal: From the tenth year of Taihe onward, edicts and patents were all the Emperor's compositions.
idiomatic: From the tenth year of Taihe onward, edicts and patents were all the emperor's compositions.

literal: His remaining essays numbered more than a hundred pieces.
idiomatic: His remaining essays numbered more than a hundred pieces.

literal: He loved the strange and valued scholars, with feeling like hunger and thirst.
idiomatic: He loved the strange and valued scholars, with feeling like hunger and thirst.

literal: Receiving court worthies, he weighed each by talent, often entrusting the intent of plain cloth.
idiomatic: Receiving court worthies, he weighed each by talent, often entrusting the intent of plain cloth.

literal: Serene and abstruse, he was not encumbered in mind by worldly affairs.
idiomatic: Serene and abstruse, he was not encumbered in mind by worldly affairs.

literal: He was also from youth skilled at archery and had physical strength.
idiomatic: He was also from youth skilled at archery and had physical strength.

literal: Past age ten he could with a finger snap apart a sheep's shoulder bone.
idiomatic: Past age ten he could with a finger snap apart a sheep's shoulder bone.

literal: When shooting birds and beasts, none failed to fall as he intended.
idiomatic: When shooting birds and beasts, none failed to fall as he intended.

literal: By age fifteen he no longer took life; shooting and hunting all ceased.
idiomatic: By age fifteen he no longer took life; shooting and hunting all ceased.

literal: His nature was frugal and plain; he regularly wore washed clothes; saddle and bridle were iron and wood only.
idiomatic: His nature was frugal and plain; he regularly wore washed clothes; saddle and bridle were iron and wood only.

literal: The Emperor's refined aims were all of this kind.
idiomatic: The emperor's refined aims were all of this kind.

literal: The historiographer states: When Wei first based itself on the northern frontier and cleared and pacified the southern Xia, opening territory for generations, all took martial might as the enterprise; matters of civil teaching had not yet been reached.
idiomatic: The historiographer states: When Wei first based itself on the northern frontier and cleared and pacified the southern Xia, opening territory for generations, all took martial might as the enterprise; matters of civil teaching had not yet been reached.

literal: Gaozu in youth inherited the great succession and early showed the wind of sagely wisdom.
idiomatic: Gaozu in youth inherited the great succession and early showed the wind of sagely wisdom.

literal: At the time Empress Dowager Wencheng held affairs, at ease and reverent, with abstruse survey alone he attained it, manifest in silence; what the divine contract marked was already in accord with hidden transformation.
idiomatic: At the time Empress Dowager Wencheng held affairs, at ease and reverent, with abstruse survey alone he attained it, manifest in silence; what the divine contract marked was already in accord with hidden transformation.

literal: When he personally held great government, ten thousand affairs a day—for more than ten years he had no leisure; different paths returned to one end, a hundred cares to one accord; as for what the living found hard to practice and the heights of human relations—though he honored the yellow house, he fully trod them.
idiomatic: When he personally held great government, ten thousand affairs a day—for more than ten years he had no leisure; different paths returned to one end, a hundred cares to one accord; as for what the living found hard to practice and the heights of human relations—though he honored the yellow house, he fully trod them.

literal: As for reverent clarity and examining antiquity, harmonizing Heaven and man, imperial regulation and court norms, weighing use and discarding—brilliantly he had culture; the black-haired people within the seas all received the gift of ear and eye.
idiomatic: As for reverent clarity and examining antiquity, harmonizing Heaven and man, imperial regulation and court norms, weighing use and discarding—brilliantly he had culture; the black-haired people within the seas all received the gift of ear and eye.

literal: Added to heroic talent and great design, loving the strange and valuing scholars, viewing those below as if wounded, taxing himself to benefit things—none could name it fully.
idiomatic: Added to heroic talent and great design, loving the strange and valuing scholars, viewing those below as if wounded, taxing himself to benefit things—none could name it fully.

literal: To weave Heaven and Earth—was the posthumous title empty?
idiomatic: To weave Heaven and Earth—was the posthumous title empty?

literal: Collation notes
idiomatic: Collation notes

literal: Yangping Wang Yi drove them off: in all editions "Yi" reads "Xi".
idiomatic: Yangping Wang Yi drove them off: in all editions "Yi" reads "Xi".

literal: Palace Edition textual verification states: "According to Xi's basic biography
idiomatic: Palace Edition textual verification states, "According to Xi's basic biography

literal: (juan 16)
idiomatic: (juan 16)

literal: he died in the sixth year of Taichang; from the fourteenth year of Taihe it was already five or six decades.
idiomatic: he died in the sixth year of Taichang; from the fourteenth year of Taihe it was already five or six decades.

literal: Examining the Treatise on Astral Portents
idiomatic: Examining the Treatise on Astral Portents
